ops.entry: WHEN a fix claims to reject malformed or foreign input DO probe each field the downstream decision reads (missing, wrong type, out-of-domain) plus an identity case (a related record from another scope) — container-shape tests reach neither a bad field value nor a shape-valid record with the wrong identity.
ops.why: LC-2+LC-3: two consecutive validate rounds missed field-level and identity classes after QA closed the container shape; displaces P-05, a dev design choice rather than a QA test action

ops.entry: WHEN fail-first needs a pre-fix red and source edits are refused DO load the old blob (`git show <sha>:<path>`) into a fresh in-process module, or check the new tests into a pin at the old SHA — either reproduces the builder's reds without touching the reviewed tree.
ops.why: observed: both methods reproduced builder red counts exactly across two cycles; displaces P-07, a narrow lock-release fixture rule

ops.entry: WHEN a fake or recorder stands in for a call DO assert both the recorded event and its selector arguments at each call site — an unasserted recorder stays green when the call is dropped, and an argument-blind fake stays green when a requested field is dropped.
ops.why: observed: a recorder lambda never asserted was blind to its call being dropped; same rule family as P-12, sharpened at equal length

ops.entry: WHEN the repository's CI runs gates the QA matrix omits (audits, route checks) DO enumerate CI's required steps and run or name each omitted one at the reviewed tip — a green matrix is not CI-green, and drift only those gates catch ships past repeated matrix_ok rounds.
ops.why: LC-1: a canonical-reader audit exited 2 at the reviewed tip after three matrix_ok rounds; displaces G-02, a ship-gate concern outside QA's seat

originals.original: WHEN a stricter consistency lock exposes a real prohibited site DO derive that site from the canonical authority rather than exempt it — an exemption preserves a parallel source of truth and lets future authority changes drift.

WHEN verifying feedback must run after a writer releases a lock DO make the fixture checker acquire the sibling lock non-blocking and assert it is free — source order or a call-only fake does not prove post-release execution.

WHEN a fake stands in for a call taking a selector argument (e.g. `fields`) DO assert the argument value at each call site, not just that the call happened — an argument-blind fake returns fixed data regardless, so dropping a field stays green while the real callee refuses the request.

WHEN a ship or merge freshness gate compares branch state DO refresh and compare against the remote default-branch authority, not local `main` — a stale local ref can let an untested conflicting change pass.

ops.entry: WHEN a perturbation proof must mutate code under .claude/skills/** DO mutate in memory (monkeypatch the in-process module; route reached-markers to sys.__stderr__, since redirect_stdout swallows print) — check-domain refuses QA source edits even inside a managed pin, and bash-write-guard denies ad hoc scratch copies.
ops.why: observed this run: check-domain refused source perturbation inside QA's own managed pin, superseding G-06's worktree-copy advice

ops.entry: WHEN running the integration kind in a fresh managed pin DO run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in the pin first — the pin has no node_modules, so tests/integration/test-typescript-typecheck.py reds on missing tsc, a false environment failure.
ops.why: observed: fresh pin reds integration until install; would otherwise be misgraded as a regression

ops.entry: WHEN redirecting output under bash-write-guard DO use a literal absolute target path — a redirect whose target contains a shell variable (e.g. `> mut-$m.txt`) is blocked even under /tmp; pipe to grep inside mutant loops instead.
ops.why: observed: variable-target redirects blocked while literal /tmp paths pass; recurs in every mutant loop

originals.original: WHEN bash-write-guard blocks a Bash-tool scratch-copy (cp/redirect) for a perturbation proof DO create a disposable git worktree under .claude/worktrees/ instead — the guard permits `git worktree add` there while denying ad hoc scratch copies elsewhere, and Bash-copy permissiveness is not reliable session to session.
